title: Algebraic-space quotient of a stack with flat inertia
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Its inertia stack $I_{\mathcal X/S}$ has objects $(x,a)$ over $T$, where $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ and $a:x\xrightarrow{\sim}x$ is an automorphism; its projection sends $(x,a)$ to $x$. Assume this projection, which is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], is flat and locally of finite presentation, tested after scheme base change on etale charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $Q$ be the fppf sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $T\mapsto\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal X(T))/\cong$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. Then $Q$ is an algebraic space and the natural map $\pi:\mathcal X\to Q$ is surjective and smooth. Here the map need not be representable: smoothness is tested on a smooth scheme atlas of the source and etale scheme charts of the target. If $\mathcal X\to S$ is smooth, then $Q\to S$ is smooth as well.

source.place: Tag 06QJ, proposition-when-gerbe; Tag 06QD, lemma-gerbe-over-iso-classes; Tag 0DN8, lemma-gerbe-smooth; literature/stacks-project/spaces-descent.tex Tag 0AHD, lemma-syntomic-smooth-etale-permanence (applied to a smooth scheme atlas).

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $u:U\to\mathcal X$ and write $x$ for its object over $U$. The etale-stack convention gives an fppf stack by [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent]. Its representable diagonal makes $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$ an algebraic space: on $T$ it consists of $(a,b,r)$ with $r:x_a\xrightarrow{\sim}x_b$. Its projections $s,t:R\to U$ are smooth and surjective by base change of the atlas, using [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Composition and inverse are composition and inverse of these isomorphisms. The subspace $G=R\times_{U\times_SU}U$ consists of automorphisms of $x$. Thus $G\to U$ is the scheme pullback of the inertia projection. The hypothesis says exactly that $G\to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation; no smoothness of $G$ is claimed.

source.place: Tag 06QJ, converse, choose smooth atlas and identify its stabilizer; Tag 06PR, lemma-presentation-inertia (objectwise identification written here).

proof.text: Let $G$ act on $R$ over $s:R\to U$ by $g\cdot r=r\circ g^{-1}$. This is a left action, since $r\circ h^{-1}\circ g^{-1}=r\circ(gh)^{-1}$. If $r\circ g^{-1}=r$, cancellation by $r^{-1}$ gives $g=1$, on every test scheme. Apply [lem-sfb-free-flat-group-space-quotient] with $B=U$ and $Z=R$. It gives an algebraic space $A=R/G$, a surjective flat locally finitely presented map $q:R\to A$, and fppf local lifts of its sections. Source and target are invariant. They descend to maps $s_A,t_A:A\to U$ by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

source.place: Tag 06QJ, converse, free stabilizer action and quotient; Bootstrap Tag 06PH, lemma-quotient-free-action.

proof.text: There is a natural isomorphism $A\cong h_U\times_Qh_U$ carrying $(s_A,t_A)$ to the two projections. Indeed, $r:x_a\to x_b$ gives equal isomorphism classes, hence the map from $R$ factors through $A$. Every section of $A$ locally lifts to such an $r$. If two lifts $r_1,r_2:x_a\to x_b$ have the same endpoints, take $g=r_2^{-1}r_1$; then $g\cdot r_1=r_2$. They therefore give the same section of $A$. This proves injectivity after a common lifting cover and then globally by its sheaf axiom. Conversely a pair $(a,b)$ in $h_U\times_Qh_U$ means the two classes $[x_a],[x_b]$ agree in the sheafification. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] they agree in the presheaf after an fppf cover, so choose local isomorphisms $r_i:x_a\to x_b$. Their images in $A$ agree on overlaps by the cancellation calculation just made, and glue uniquely. The glued section has endpoints $(a,b)$. Pullbacks preserve this construction because the local formulas and the unique gluings do. This proves the claimed natural isomorphism, including for nonreduced test schemes.

source.place: Tag 06QJ, converse, monomorphism of the quotient relation; Tag 06QD, lemma-gerbe-over-iso-classes, local equality of isomorphism classes.

proof.text: The maps $s_A,t_A$ are smooth. Here is the chart argument for $s_A$, avoiding any assumption that $q$ is smooth. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $W\to A$, form $R_W=R\times_AW$, and choose a surjective etale scheme chart $Z\to R_W$. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $Z\to W$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Also $Z\to R$ is etale, so $Z\to R\xrightarrow{s}U$ is smooth by the same calculus and step 1. Both $W$ and $U$ are schemes. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] to $Z\to W\to U$ to conclude $W\to U$ smooth. The etale-chart definition of smoothness then gives $s_A$ smooth. The identical argument with $t$ gives $t_A$ smooth. Both are surjective because the identity arrows give a section $U\to A$ of each; a point of $U$ lifts along that section. They are consequently flat and locally of finite presentation by the cited calculus.

source.place: Tag 06QJ, converse, descent through the stabilizer quotient, strengthened to smoothness by the chart argument of Tag 0DLS, lemma-smooth-quotient-stack; spaces-descent.tex Tag 0AHE, lemma-smooth-permanence.

proof.text: The map $h_U\to Q$ has fppf local lifts of sections. For $a\in Q(T)$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] supplies an fppf cover and objects $y_i\in\mathcal X(T_i)$ whose classes represent $a$. The base changes $V_i=T_i\times_{\mathcal X}U\to T_i$ are smooth surjective algebraic spaces by the atlas definition. By [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections], after an etale covering of each $T_i$ they have sections, giving maps to $U$ whose objects are isomorphic to the restrictions of $y_i$. Etale maps are flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], so these refinements are fppf coverings in [def-pc-fppf-site]. Composing covering families gives an fppf covering $\{T_j\to T\}$ and maps $a_j:T_j\to U$ representing $a|_{T_j}$.

source.place: Tag 06QD, local surjectivity argument; Tag 06QJ, the smooth atlas and the fppf quotient.

proof.text: For this $a\in Q(T)$ put $F_a=h_T\times_Qh_U$, a sheaf over $T$. On a lifting cover from step 5 its restriction is $T_j\times_{a_j,U,s_A}A$: a pair $(a_j,b)$ in the relation of step 3 is exactly the equality $a|_{T_j}=[x_b]$. These are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and their projections to $T_j$ are smooth surjective by step 4 and [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality]. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-local-algebraic-space] to get an algebraic space representing $F_a$. Its size hypothesis is satisfied in the chosen universes: use a covering with at most one member per point of $T$, obtained by retaining for each point one member containing it, and choose all its charts in the same containing universe. Their set-indexed scheme coproduct exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and lies within the site bound [def-weil-size-convention]. The fppf target locality in [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality] now makes $F_a\to T$ smooth and surjective. This applies to every scheme $T$ and every $a$.

source.place: Tag 06QJ, algebraicity of the quotient relation and Bootstrap; fppf descent of the atlas fibres as in the proof of Tag 0DLS.

proof.text: Thus $h_U\to Q$ is representable by algebraic spaces, smooth and surjective, by the scheme tests of step 6. In particular it is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Since $Q$ is an fppf sheaf by construction, [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap] applies and makes $Q$ an algebraic space. The composite of the chosen smooth scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X$ with $\pi$ is precisely this smooth surjective morphism $U\to Q$. Consequently $\pi$ is smooth in the nonrepresentable atlas sense stated in the item. It is surjective: the local lifts to $U$ in step 5 are objects of $\mathcal X$ over those covers. We have proved this with an arbitrary smooth atlas, so no choice of atlas has entered the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 06QJ, final Bootstrap step; Tags 06QD and 0DN8, identification with the isomorphism-class sheaf and smooth surjectivity.

proof.text: Finally assume $\mathcal X\to S$ smooth. Choose the atlas $U\to\mathcal X$ with $U\to S$ smooth, as allowed by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Steps 1--7 give $U\to Q$ smooth and surjective for this atlas. For a surjective etale scheme chart $V\to Q$, the fibre product $W=U\times_QV$ is a scheme because the diagonal of $Q$ is representable, as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $W\to V$ is smooth surjective, hence flat and locally of finite presentation, and $W\to U$ is etale. Thus $W\to S$ is smooth. Applying [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] to $W\to V\to S$ shows that $V\to S$ is smooth. The etale-chart test gives smoothness of $Q\to S$. This also covers empty stacks and the empty quotient.
